_doc: Findings ('what the data shows') contract. Rendered by harness/build_essays.py into <section id='findings'>. {{fact:KEY}} tokens are replaced at build time with live figures from harness/findings_facts.compute_facts(), so this prose stays true to the current data. Methodology: contract/findings_writing.json. {{cite:KEY}} resolve to numbered footnotes.

blocks.text: A model is only interesting if it sees something. The current index is a provisional slice of {{fact:total}} entities across {{fact:n_layers}} layers ({{fact:l1}} carriers, {{fact:l2}} MGAs/brokers, {{fact:l3}} assets, {{fact:l4}} tail), scored largely at the assessed tier while the live registers are loaded — so what follows is a read of structure, not a published ranking. The blended measured share is {{fact:measured_pct}}, below the 60% publication gate. The point is not yet the magnitudes. It is that the shape the model was built to detect is already legible in the data.

blocks.caption: Distribution of the current universe across the four quadrants, on median cut-lines (exposure ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, preparedness ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}).

blocks.text: Three things stand out even on this slice. First, the field is not uniformly exposed: {{fact:earning_count}} entities ({{fact:earning_pct}}) sit in Earning it and {{fact:sidelined_count}} ({{fact:sidelined_pct}}) in Sidelined, with only {{fact:exposed_count}} ({{fact:exposed_pct}}) in the outright danger zone — {{fact:exposed_names}}. That is exactly the pattern a damage-only view would miss, because it flags as fine an entity whose exposure to non-firm power is invisible to its own wordings.

Second, the spread between the most and least prepared is wide and interpretable. The largest positive Margin of Safety belongs to {{fact:top_mos_name}} (Margin {{fact:top_mos_val}}), whose preparedness — rated capital, named availability capability — runs well ahead of the exposure it has taken on. The most negative belongs to {{fact:low_mos_name}} (Margin {{fact:low_mos_val}}), an entity whose non-firm intensity sits ahead of any visible mitigation. The model is not asserting these are good or bad businesses; it is locating each on the one axis that matters for this peril — whether the bet is matched by the means to carry it.

Third, there is genuine whitespace: {{fact:whitespace_count}} entities including {{fact:whitespace_names}} sit in the capable-but-under-deployed quadrant. On the thesis of this index, that is where the unwritten availability cover should originate — underwriters with the capital and competence to carry the risk who are not yet earning on it.{{cite:ACAD-CLARKE-INDEX-DEMAND}}

The peril does not distribute evenly across the value chain. Exposed concentrates in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}} — {{fact:exposed_l3_names}} among the asset names — which is structurally right: non-firm intensity is a register fact at Layer 3 before it propagates upward into carrier books. Carriers and MGAs show up more often in Whitespace ({{fact:whitespace_l1}} at Layer 1, {{fact:whitespace_l2}} at Layer 2) and Sidelined than in Exposed, because preparedness inputs (capital, product fit, specialist teams) are easier to evidence at balance-sheet layers than curtailment exposure is to see from the outside.

Layer 1 still contributes {{fact:exposed_l1}} Exposed names — carriers whose book concentration and trigger gap outrun parametric or availability product fit. That is a different failure mode from the asset case: not “curtailed tomorrow” but “writing damage-only cover on a peril whose loss is lawful switch-off.”{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI}}
Where exposure runs ahead of preparedness

Within Exposed, the deepest negative margin is {{fact:worst_exposed_name}} (Margin {{fact:worst_exposed_mos}}). Of {{fact:l3_total}} scored assets, {{fact:gate_firm_count}} have a firm Gate register status and {{fact:gate_unknown_count}} remain unknown pending a Gate-2 record — the index shows the number but does not infer firmness. The honest read is that the L3 Exposed cluster ({{fact:exposed_l3}} of {{fact:exposed_count}}) is directionally right while magnitudes and ordering will move as NESO and DNO registers are fully ingested.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-TEC}}

The headline finding is not a ranking. It is that exposure and preparedness genuinely come apart — across {{fact:total}} entities and {{fact:mos_spread}} points of margin spread — which is the whole reason a one-axis hazard score would mislead, and a margin would not.
What would change, and what would not

The blended measured share is {{fact:measured_pct}}, well below the 60% publication gate, so the index is labelled PROVISIONAL and should be read as direction, not measurement. What moves as the live data lands is the magnitude and ordering within each quadrant: as non-firm intensity is pulled from the connection registers and capital from the filings, entities will shift across the median cut-lines (currently exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}) and the rank order will firm up. What does not change is the construct — the two axes, the margin, and the finding that they separate. The honest version of this section will be re-run automatically on every build, against whatever the registers then say.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}}
